item.title: Carolina Science Cafe: Who’s a Journalist in the Age of AI? — Tue Oct 6, 6:00 PM — Haw River Tap & Table
item.description:
Who’s a Journalist in the Age of AI?
Theorizing Distributed Journalistic Authority Amid Newsfluencers, Algorithms, and Generative Systems
Who’s a Journalist in the Age of AI? addresses a critical development in the news media. In this talk, UNC-Chapel Hill’s Hussman School of Journalism and Media faculty member, Deb Aikat, PhD, will discuss how generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) reconfigures the epistemic boundaries of journalistic authority, credibility, and public verification in democratic discourse.
Dr. Aikat will discuss how AI is reshaping press freedom at a time when public trust in media has sunk to 28%, according to Gallup’s 2025 survey. He studies the shifting information landscape in the U.S. and India — the world’s oldest and largest democracies — tracing how digital platforms empower people to publish, protest, and participate in civic life beyond traditional newsrooms.
Carolina Science Cafe is a free program by Morehead Planetarium and Science Center

item.description:
Dr. Davaalkham's presentation covers climate change, which is warming Mongolia three times faster than the global average, and severe air pollution, estimated to cause 9.7% of all deaths in the city. It also covers heavy metals in drinking water, poor sanitation, and soil contamination from more than 200,000 pit latrines. It then reviews national laws, the updated air quality standard, surveillance systems, and strategies for building workforce and research capacity. It ends with the NIH-funded Mongolian GEOHealth Center (U01/U2R, 2022-2027), a partnership with Duke University and UTMB, and its results so far: 20 fellows trained, graduate students supported, and research papers published.

item.title: Towards Personalizing Assistive Technology in the Real World — Wed Oct 7, 3:45 PM — Teer 106
item.description:
Abstract: Assistive technology offers promise to improve personal mobility for hundreds of millions of people. However, determining how to assist people to accommodate their unique needs across everyday mobility scenarios is an open challenge. Personalizing assistance to each user has helped meet these needs and systematically improve mobility outcomes in laboratory settings. To address these challenges, our group performs biomechanical studies to understand people's movement goals and needs, develops real-world personalization methods, and applies these findings to assist patient populations including people post-stroke, people with knee osteoarthritis, and people with blindness.
Dr. Patrick Slade is an Assistant Professor of Bioengineering at Harvard University.

item.title: Compositional Systems Biology: An Executable Framework for Connecting Models Across Scales — Thu Oct 8, 10:00 AM — None
item.description: Abstract: Biological systems are organized across interacting scales, from molecular networks and metabolic pathways to cells, tissues, microbial communities, and their environments, yet many computational models remain difficult to connect, reuse, or extend beyond the scale or formalism for which they were originally built. In this talk, I will introduce Compositional Systems Biology, an approach for building multiscale biological models from interoperable processes with explicit interfaces, shared state representations, and well-defined orchestration patterns governing when and how model components are executed. At the core of this work is Vivarium, an open-source platform for multiscale simulation that integrates diverse modeling formalisms -- including ODEs, stochastic kinetics, constraint-based models, agent-based dynamics, and rule-based logic -- within a unified execution framework. item.title: Protect Your Thinking: Smarter Habits for Working with AI — Thu Oct 15, 9:00 AM — 79 Degrees West
item.description:
AI isn't going away, so the real question is whether it's making you sharper or making you soft. New research shows that people who use AI to hand them finished answers actually get worse at the underlying skill once the AI is taken away. But people who use AI for hints, critique, and sharpening their own explanations keep those gains a week later.
This session is for anyone who's wondered what AI is really doing to the way we think.
Source: UNC Chapel Hill

item.title: Aging Gracefully Creative Movement Workshop — Wed Oct 21, 11:00 AM — Arts Together
item.description:
Ages 50+ Aging Gracefully: Meaningful Movement Explorations – As we age it is important to keep the body moving, the brain focused, and the spirit fueled. In this technique/creative dance class, we will do so in a healthy, FUN way. We will warm the body, moving in a way that encourages each dancer to better honor and understand their unique physicality. Next, dancers will explore different ways to generate movement phrases. Inspired by poetry, visual art, and personal experience, we will create dances; accessing the wisdom of the body to express our relationship to the world, each other, and ourselves. No prior dance experience needed, just a willing heart <3
Source: United Arts Wake County

item.title: Dedications & Commemorations of the Battle of New Garden — Sat Oct 24, 9:30 AM — Multiple locations see itinerary for details
item.description:
Please join Cricket Crigler, State Regent of the North Carolina Society of the Daughters of the American Revolution, and Gloria Halstead, State Historian, along with eight sponsoring chapters, for the dedication of five commemorative markers honoring the Battle of New Garden on October 24 and 25.
Sponsoring Chapters:
Alexander Martin ChapterBattle of Alamance ChapterColonel Arthur Forbis ChapterColonel Joseph Winston ChapterDeep River ChapterGuilford Battle ChapterRachel Caldwell ChapterWilliam Bethell ChapterThe dedication ceremonies are free and open to the public. Five markers will be placed commemorating the three engagements that comprise the Battle of New Garden — the engagement in the lane, the engagement at the meeting house, and the engagement at the crossroads — as well as the encampments of General Nathanael Greene and General Charles Cornwallis.

item.title: Reynolda on the House — Sun Oct 25, 1:30 PM — Reynolda House Museum of American Art
item.description:
Upcoming Date and Time(s): Oct 25, 2026, 1:30pm — 4:30pm
Nov 15, 2026, 1:30pm — 4:30pm
Location: Reynolda House Museum of American Art
Cost: Free to attend
All are welcome to visit Reynolda “On the House”!
We invite you to enjoy the exhibitions Flash Point: The Civil Rights Photography of Danny Lyon and Art & Democracy.
One of the oldest forms of storytelling in the United States is puppetry, used for entertainment, education, and political statement. To celebrate this facet of American creative ingenuity, Reynolda welcomes Paperhand Puppets, a puppetry arts organization, performing World of Wonder, a whimsical and interactive showcase of creatures and characters from Paperhand’s 26 year history that celebrates the wild wisdom of our world.
Made possible in part by a grant from America 250 NC, an initiative by the North Carolina Department of Natural and Cultural Resources.
